lead.t: Vascular compliance (aorta, pulmonary artery): Pulse pressure is the difference between systolic and diastolic pressures; compliance determines pulse wave velocity. — Aortic regurgitation reduces compliance → wide pulse pressure, water‑hammer pulse, and peripheral pulsations.

snip.t: Vascular compliance (aorta, pulmonary artery): Pulse pressure is the difference between systolic and diastolic pressures; compliance determines pulse wave velocity. — Aortic regurgitation reduces compliance → wide pulse pressure, water‑hammer pulse, and peripheral pulsations.

Carotid and femoral arteries: Reflection of pulse wave; arterial stiffness alters wave timing. — Corrigan’s sign (carotid pulsation) and Traube’s sign (femoral “pistol‑shot” sound) are classic for aortic regurgitation.
Rheumatic heart disease: This is a significant cause of valvular damage, particularly mitral and aortic regurgitation, creating a substrate for IE.
*New or changing murmur:* Regurgitant murmurs (mitral or aortic regurgitation) caused by leaflet perforation, tear, or bulky vegetations impeding coaptation.
In aortic regurgitation, the pathology is either destruction of the cusps or root dilatation
